text.p: Tabcorp Holdings Ltd managing director Ross Wilson said he expects the gaming and wagering group to record a good profit rise in the year to June 30, 1997. "I think that there is some growth there if we can drive it, and we if we can do that and we can get our fair share of it. Then we will expect to see good profit increases again next year," Wilson told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"But I must say that we are not immune to the economy and I think the economy is looking fairly lacklustre and for that reason we will hopefully achieve our goal of being better than the average improvements," Wilson said.

Tabcorp earlier reported a 27.3 percent rise in net profit to A$87.17 million for the 1995/96 year compared with a year earlier. Tabcorp also paid a special 12 cent dividend on top of its 10 cents dividend, making a year total of 31 cents.
Wilson said Tabcorp would keep its current payout ratio. "With a company like ours with a strong cash flow, a 70 percent payout ratio is not out of the question," Wilson said.

"I don't see a lot of mileage for company's holding back the cash unless they can justify in doing so. We feel now with our forecast cash requirements we can justifiably pay out the special dividend without any difficulties," Wilson said.
Wilson did not rule out further special dividend payments, but only if it did not stop the group from making acquisitions.
"Obviously we shall assess the position," Wilson said.
"But at the same time we do not in any way diminish our potential to go forward and do other things," he said.

"We are still looking at opportunities and if opportunities arise that make sense from a shareholders point of view, we will embark on them," he said. "We will look into state and we will look overseas if the opportunties are there," Wilson said.
He said Tabcorp has funding capabilities of about A$500 million to fund any potential acquisitions.
"If you look at our balance sheet and look at our cash flow strength, there is a funding ability there well in excees of A$500 million, without any difficulty," Wilson said.
"I'm not saying we are going to use that or more than that."

He said the group, which was privatised by the Victorian government in August 1994, was looking at potential purchases in the leisure and entertainment industry, including, gaming and wagering related businesses.
He said Tabcorp had stated it would take two years after privatisation before it would start making acquisitions as it had been focused on internal issues over the past two years.
Wilson said he expects sales growth to continue to be strong as Australia's gambling sector continued to grow faster than the the nation's economy over the next few years.
Tabcorp, which mainly operates in Victoria, reported a 17.9 percent rise in sales revenue to A$733.7 million in 1995/96.
"We see the Australian gambling business still growing at a rate faster than GDP, at least to the year 2000 and beyond and we see a similar story in Victoria," Wilson said.
He said total gambling in Victoria increased by 18 percent in the 1995/96 year. Victorians currently spend A$2.6 billion on gambling, he said.
Wilson said Tabcorp might feel some affect from the opening of the A$1.6 billion Melbourne pernament casino in February 1997. Crown Ltd operate the Melbourne casino.
"It will have an affect and one can't deny that. How great it will be. I don't really know, but I don't think it will be that great quite frankly," Wilson said.
The special dividend helped boost Tabcorp shares to a record high on Monday.
At 1.55 p.m. (0355 GMT), Tabcorp shares were 16 cents higher at A$5.93, off the record high of A$6.00 briefing touched during Monday's trade. -- Kevin Morrison, Sydney 61-2 9373-1800
